01 · Case study · Data Platform

35% faster pipelines. ~20% lower compute cost.

A production data platform running across Microsoft Fabric and Databricks, serving finance and operational workloads. Over time it had accumulated orchestration and compute overhead — slow to run, expensive to keep running, still responsible for the same datasets on the same schedule.

35%

faster pipeline execution

~20%

lower compute cost

50+

stakeholders served

Context

The platform grew organically. Pipelines, schedules, and compute choices piled up over time. Sources included ERP, leasing, and finance systems; downstream, 50+ stakeholders depended on the datasets for daily decisions.

Constraint

Runtime and cost had to come down without touching reliability. Same datasets, same schedule, same guarantees — less waiting, less spend.

Architecture

Decision

Orchestration was redesigned and compute simplified: fewer moving parts, less redundant processing, workloads sized and scheduled for what they actually needed. Nothing exotic — mostly removing work the system didn't need to do.

Result

Pipeline runtime down 35%. Compute cost down ~20%. Same datasets, same reliability, a third less waiting.

Overhead accumulates silently on platforms that work. Nobody schedules it; it just compounds.

Nothing exotic — mostly removing work the system didn't need to do.

Lessons

  1. Overhead accumulates silently on platforms that work. Nobody schedules it; it just compounds.
  2. Removing unnecessary work beats optimizing necessary work.
  3. Cost and runtime are engineering constraints, not finance's problem to discover later.

Stack

Microsoft Fabric · Databricks · Spark
